summary: Harness usage and limits replicate only when they change what readers answer: usage at rest waits for its interval or the next turn end, and a seat's limits report that does not change its account's answer stays in the local observation log

replay.detail: Fewer harness.usage and harness.limits claims are written; nothing already in the graph is rewritten or re-read differently. A seat's harness.limits report replicates only when the seat names an account it has no reading for, when it would change the account's chosen reading, or when the account has measured nothing newer for 15 minutes (LIMITS_REFRESH_MS); any other report stays in the host's local observation log and never becomes a claim. A seat's usage that arrives while its harness rests replicates as its first reading since the harness stopped working, at the next turn end, or once 5 minutes (USAGE_PUBLISH_INTERVAL_MS) have passed since the slot last replicated (on the harness's next state re-stamp); a harness that never reports a state replicates every reading, as before.

schema.detail: No schema change: the existing local observation log and latest-slot tables hold the readings that do not replicate.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: No claim kind, field, wire or CLI contract changes, and old claims are untouched. On other nodes an account's limits reading can be up to 15 minutes older than before (well inside the hour after which the limits policy and st slo ls call a reading stale), and a seat's usage that arrived at rest can be up to 5 minutes older; st usage --json, the usage budgets in st slo ls, the limits policy and its 90%/95% seat pauses and the apps read the same answers. A mixed-version fleet keeps working: an older node keeps replicating every report and a newer node reads its claims as before, and the newer node's fewer claims are ordinary claims to an older reader.

downtime.detail: No restart beyond the normal upgrade; no migration or backfill.

recovery.detail: No data recovery is needed. Reverting restores replicating every report from the next reading; the readings that stayed local remain in each host's local observation log and the replicated answers were the same.
